$comment: AUTHORITATIVE CONTRACT SOURCE OF TRUTH. Hand-edited. Everything under packages/contracts/generated/ is derived from this file by tools/generate.py. See ADR-009.

identifiers.name: UserId
identifiers.description: A principal. Not a tenant. See ADR-005.

identifiers.name: WorkspaceId
identifiers.description: The tenant boundary. Required on every tenant-scoped contract.

identifiers.name: ResearchProjectId
identifiers.description: Persistent workspace-scoped research objective. Ontology V2 §11.2.

identifiers.name: ResearchSessionId
identifiers.description: The only persisted execution entity. Ontology V2 §11.4. Replaces the retired 'run_id'.

identifiers.name: OpportunityId
identifiers.description: A domain hypothesis. Not owned by the session that found it. Ontology V2 §12.

identifiers.name: ClaimId
identifiers.description: An assertion about an Opportunity that evidence can independently support or contradict. Ontology V2.1 §17. STABLE across statement revisions: the text may be rewritten, the identity may not. Distinct from ClaimType, which is an epistemic category and not an identity.

identifiers.name: EvidenceId
identifiers.description: An evidence record with mandatory provenance.

identifiers.name: SourceId
identifiers.description: A registered external source. Global, not tenant-scoped. Registry contents are D-07, still open.

closed_enums.name: ClaimType
closed_enums.description: How an analytical statement is supported. Never conflated in any output.

values.description: Directly supported by collected evidence
Derived analytically from one or more observations
A model-generated estimate about an unknown or future outcome
A proposed action or decision generated by the system
A plausible proposition that currently lacks sufficient evidence

closed_enums.name: MarketScopeType
closed_enums.description: Geographic scope discriminator. Geographic axis only; segment scoping is A-12 and is NOT modelled.

values.description: No geographic restriction
One or more region registry identifiers
Exactly one national market
Aggregate across two or more named markets

closed_enums.name: ResearchSessionStatus
closed_enums.description: Session lifecycle. Budget exhaustion is COMPLETED with reduced Research Completeness, never a status. A session that finds nothing is COMPLETED, not FAILED.

values.description: Accepted, not yet planned
Building the research plan and budget
Acquisition in progress
NLP, market intelligence, competition
Score families being computed
Finished, whether coverage was complete or partial
Could not produce a usable result
Stopped on request

closed_enums.name: DemandSignalFamily
closed_enums.description: Closed. Signal TYPES within a family are a registry, not an enum.

values.description: Complaint, frustration, workaround, missing feature
Explicit request, wish, expressed intent
Engagement, repeated usage, purchases
Launches, funding, search growth, platform change

closed_enums.name: ScoreFamily
closed_enums.description: The five families. Never collapsed into a single number, not in an API, a sort key or a badge.

values.description: How attractive, given the research context
How strong and diverse the supporting evidence is
How feasible under the requested constraints
How much of the relevant space was examined
How confident the model is in its interpretation. A SCORE on 0-100, not a confidence field.

closed_enums.name: LlmTier
closed_enums.description: Logical tier. Business services request a tier, never a provider or model name.

values.description: High-volume, cheap, low-latency
Default reasoning
Complex synthesis and planning
Vector embeddings

closed_enums.name: RegistryStatus
closed_enums.description: Deprecation, never deletion. A deprecated entry stops being offered for new classification but keeps resolving for historical records.

values.description: Available for new classification
Historical only

closed_enums.name: SourceApprovalState
closed_enums.description: Where a source stands in the governance gate. Closed: collector eligibility branches exhaustively on it, and an unhandled value would mean a source of unknown standing being treated as usable. Public visibility never produces APPROVED on its own.

values.description: A candidate has been recorded. No review has been attempted
Review started and could not conclude. The correct result whenever terms are ambiguous, unreachable or silent. Never convert uncertainty into permission
Permitted only while the recorded conditions hold. The conditions are part of the approval, not advice
Permitted for the assessed activities, supported by evidence. Requires at least one evidence record
Some assessed activity is not permitted. Not collector-eligible until the restriction is lifted or the activity is narrowed
Documented terms forbid the intended use. A terminal judgment for the assessed scope, revisited only by a new review
Operationally halted regardless of review state. An immediate stop that does not wait for a review cycle

closed_enums.name: ConditionVerification
closed_enums.description: HOW a review condition can be checked. Exists so APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS cannot silently mean 'a collector may run': each condition is satisfied individually, and one that no machine can verify must say so rather than pretending it can.

values.description: A named configuration key is present in the environment. The KEY name, never its value
A named product capability is implemented and enabled -- for example a surface that can display a required attribution notice
A retention limit at or below a stated number of days is configured for the source
Collection uses only a named access method, and no other
No machine can check it. A person must record the decision and the reference to it. Marking this satisfied is a human act, and the honest answer for anything a program cannot establish

closed_enums.name: ConditionVerificationResult
closed_enums.description: The outcome of running a verifier against one review condition. Four values rather than a boolean, because 'we could not establish it' and 'it does not hold' call for different next steps and only one of them is a bug. UNKNOWN never becomes SATISFIED, and only SATISFIED clears the condition.

values.description: The verifier established the condition holds, and recorded what it looked at
The verifier ran and the condition does not hold. A definite answer, not an absence of one
The verifier could not establish either answer -- no verifier is registered for the condition, or what it needs to inspect is unavailable. Blocks exactly like UNSATISFIED and must never be promoted
The condition does not apply in this context, for a reason the record states. Blocks: a condition that does not apply has still not been satisfied

closed_enums.name: AttributionElement
closed_enums.description: One required part of a source's attribution obligation. A closed enum because the renderer branches exhaustively: an element it does not recognise must be a contract change, never a silently dropped requirement.

values.description: Credit to the source, in the wording the source's own terms require
The licence the resource is distributed under, named so a reader can find it
A sentence whose wording is prescribed by the terms and must appear verbatim. Never paraphrased, never composed
A statement of what was changed, required where the licence requires changes to be indicated. Includes translation
The persistent identifier of the specific dataset used. A per-resource value; it cannot be defaulted
The date the data was retrieved. A per-retrieval value; it cannot be defaulted
A disclaimer the terms require alongside modified data, supplied as text rather than composed by this system when the exact wording is not in the recorded evidence

closed_enums.name: AcquisitionErrorCode
closed_enums.description: Why an acquisition attempt did not produce records. A closed vocabulary so the orchestrator branches on a meaning rather than on a third party's exception class -- an upstream library changing its exception hierarchy must not change how this system retries. Each value also fixes whether it is worth retrying, which is the decision that costs money when it is wrong.

values.description: No acquisition authorization could be built for the source. Never retried: the answer comes from the governance gate and will not change on its own
The source is authorised and this specific resource is not -- excluded dataset, licence outside the allowlist, third-party or unestablished origin. Never retried
The request did not complete within its connect or read budget. Retryable
The source signalled too many requests. Retryable, and more slowly than other failures
The source failed in a way it describes as its own and transient. Retryable
The source rejected the request deterministically. Never retried: the same request produces the same rejection, and repeating it is how a rate limit becomes a ban
The response arrived and does not have the documented shape. Never retried: a source that changed its contract needs a person, not another attempt
The response could not be read at all -- malformed encoding or unparseable body. Never retried
Records were acquired and could not be stored. Retryable, because the source is not the problem
The job was cancelled or ran out of its bounds before completing. Never retried automatically

closed_enums.name: ResourceContentOrigin
closed_enums.description: Whether the platform's own licence covers a particular resource. Aggregators republish material they do not own, so platform approval is not resource approval. UNKNOWN exists because it is the common case and must fail closed rather than be guessed either way.

values.description: The platform produces or licenses this resource, and the reviewed terms cover it
Owned by someone other than the platform. The platform's approval grants nothing over it, and separate permission from the owner is required
Not established. Denied wherever licensing scope matters: an unexamined resource is not a resource known to be covered

closed_enums.name: RightsBasis
closed_enums.description: What kind of thing authorises one resource. Closed because authorization branches exhaustively on it and an unhandled value would mean a resource of unknown standing being treated as authorised. Two values, deliberately: there is no UNKNOWN member, because an unestablished basis is the ABSENCE of one -- expressed as null and refused -- and a third value that looked like an answer would be the exact fabrication this enum exists to prevent. A DIRECT_GRANT never satisfies a rule that requires a NAMED_LICENCE.

values.description: A published instrument authorises the resource and has an identifier that can be matched against an allowlist -- CC-BY-4.0, ODbL-1.0. The licence field is required and must name it

The source's own terms grant the use directly, naming no instrument. GDELT grants 'unlimited and unrestricted use ... of any kind without fee' and publishes no licence, so there is nothing to name; the licence field must be ABSENT rather than filled with an invented identifier, and the prose basis carries which grant it was

closed_enums.name: SourceAccessMethod
closed_enums.description: HOW access is technically performed. It says nothing about whether access is PERMITTED: permission is a separate dimension carried by the policy review. BROWSER_AUTOMATION being available never implies it is allowed.

values.description: A documented API the source operator offers for this purpose
An unauthenticated endpoint reachable without registration
A syndication feed published for consumption
A published bulk dataset or export
HTTP retrieval of pages intended for human readers. Visibility is not permission
A driven browser. Never a way around an API restriction, a login, a rate limit or an anti-automation measure
A human supplies the data. No automated access occurs

closed_enums.name: PolicyAssessment
closed_enums.description: The verdict for ONE activity. Activities are assessed separately because their conditions differ: a source may permit automated API access and forbid commercial use. A single boolean called `allowed` would erase exactly that difference.

values.description: Documented terms permit it explicitly. Requires evidence
Permitted while stated conditions hold. The conditions are recorded, not summarised away
Documented terms forbid it explicitly
The documents reviewed are silent. Silence is not permission and never becomes PERMITTED without a human decision
The documents address it ambiguously. The correct result when a reading requires legal judgment this system must not make
Nobody has looked yet

closed_enums.name: PolicyEvidenceType
closed_enums.description: What kind of document supports an assessment. Ordered by the evidence hierarchy: official operator documentation outranks anything else, and nothing below OFFICIAL_* may support an APPROVED state on its own.

values.description: Developer or API reference published by the operator
Terms of service, developer terms or API terms
A data licence or copyright/reuse statement
Privacy or data-use documentation
robots.txt or a comparable published access directive
Written confirmation from the operator, for example a granted commercial-use request
A qualified human review recorded against this source. The only type that may carry a legal conclusion

closed_enums.name: SourceLifecycle
closed_enums.description: Whether the source itself still exists as a target. Separate from approval: a deprecated source may have been approved, and an active source may never have been reviewed.

values.description: The source exists and is a candidate
Retired. Kept, never deleted, so historical provenance still resolves

closed_enums.name: SourceAcquisitionCost
closed_enums.description: The shape of what access costs, not an amount. Concrete prices are versioned configuration because operators change them; a price compiled in here would be wrong within months and would look authoritative.

values.description: No charge documented
No charge within a documented quota
A fixed or subscription charge
Charged per request, row or unit
Not documented, or not checked. Never assumed to be FREE

closed_enums.name: PersonalDataRisk
closed_enums.description: How likely the source is to carry personal data. A RISK CLASSIFICATION, not a legal ruling: it records what must be handled carefully and what still needs jurisdiction-specific review. GDPR analysis is separate and remains a human decision.

values.description: Aggregate or institutional data with no individual attribution
User-generated content under handles rather than real names
Real names, profiles or contact details may appear
Special-category information may appear in free text. Requires review before any collection
Not assessed. Never treated as NONE_EXPECTED

closed_enums.name: EvidenceDirection
closed_enums.description: How one Evidence record bears on a Claim. Support and contradiction are aggregated SEPARATELY and never averaged together, so this drives exhaustive branching and is closed.

values.description: The evidence bears in favour of the claim
The evidence bears against the claim
Related to the claim but bearing neither way. Retained for provenance and coverage; contributes to neither support nor contradiction strength

closed_enums.name: EvidenceIndependenceState
closed_enums.description: What is KNOWN about an evidence record provenance relationship to the rest of the set. UNKNOWN is a distinct third state and is never silently promoted to KNOWN_INDEPENDENT.

values.description: Provenance was established and does not derive from another record in the set
Provenance was established and shares an origin with other records; requires an independence group id
Provenance was not established. Conservative handling: all such records for one claim and one direction form at most ONE contribution group

closed_enums.name: EvidenceObservationCategory
closed_enums.description: WHAT KIND of thing was observed, independent of how strong it is. Gates EvidenceLevel 4 and 5, which quantity of evidence must never reach on its own. Closed because level eligibility branches exhaustively over it.

values.description: Someone expressed a view. A comment, a post, a reply
An account of behaviour, not the behaviour itself
Aggregated behavioural measurement: search interest, download counts, review volume
Economic activity: purchases, subscriptions, pricing, established competing products, adoption. Required for EvidenceLevel 4
Validation of THIS opportunity: interviews, signups, prototype usage, preorders, payments. Required for EvidenceLevel 5
Not categorised. Cannot lift EvidenceLevel above 3, because an uncategorised record has not been shown to be market evidence

closed_enums.name: ClaimTemporality
closed_enums.description: Whether a claim decays. A property of the CLAIM, never of the source: the same platform can carry an evergreen fact and a trend that is stale in a week. Closed because freshness branches exhaustively over it.

values.description: The claim does not decay with the passage of time. Freshness is 1.0 unless the underlying fact itself became obsolete, which is a new contradicting observation rather than decay
The claim loses force as its observations age. Requires an authorised half-life in the aggregation profile; without one the evidence is NON-SCORABLE rather than assumed fresh

closed_enums.name: ClaimOrigin
closed_enums.description: What PROCESS produced the claim, at the level of kind rather than instance. Deliberately carries no model, provider or prompt name: those change constantly and belong in provenance columns, where a new one does not require a contract change.

values.description: Authored by a person
Produced by a rule, parser or query with no model involved
Extracted from source text by a language model. The model and prompt versions are recorded in provenance, never here
Derived analytically from other claims or signals rather than read from a source
Created by the platform itself, for example a coverage placeholder
Brought in from an external dataset or a prior system

closed_enums.name: ClaimLifecycle
closed_enums.description: EDITORIAL state, never epistemic. There is deliberately no VALIDATED or REJECTED value: evidence can change, and a lifecycle state derived from EvidenceLevel would freeze a conclusion the evidence no longer supports (Mission 1.2 §38). What a claim is worth is read from its aggregation, never from this column.

values.description: In use. Accumulates evidence and may be aggregated
Removed from use — malformed, duplicated, or out of scope. Its evidence and revision history are retained, because deleting the row would destroy the record of what was once believed

closed_enums.name: ObservationKind
closed_enums.description: How one ResearchSession related to a persisted entity it encountered. Promoted to the canonical contract in Mission 1.2: it already governed opportunity observations as a SQL CHECK plus a Python frozenset, which is exactly the drift ADR-009 exists to prevent. Not a scoring judgement.

values.description: The session introduced it
The session found further support for it
The session found evidence against it

closed_enums.name: AggregationProfileStatus
closed_enums.description: Whether the PARAMETERS of a profile have been calibrated against data. Separate from whether the algorithm is defined: defining equations calibrates nothing. Production scoring requires CALIBRATED.

values.description: Being written. Not runnable
Parameters are structural or provisional, never fitted to labelled data. Runnable only in an explicitly labelled experimental mode
Parameters were fitted and evaluated against a recorded calibration dataset
Superseded. Kept so historical results stay readable

closed_enums.name: EvidenceAggregationStatus
closed_enums.description: Whether the numbers in a result may be read as covering the evidence set. A result that silently dropped half its items would be indistinguishable from one that used all of them.

values.description: Every evidence record in the snapshot was scorable
At least one record was scorable and at least one was not. missing_requirements names what was absent
No record was scorable. There is no Evidence Score, and an absent score is not a score of zero

closed_enums.name: NormalizedRecordQuality
closed_enums.description: The STRUCTURAL completeness of a normalized record, and nothing else. Not a confidence and not a reliability: those are epistemic judgments on [0,1] that belong to the evidence model, and a value of that kind here would invite a downstream stage to multiply a parsing outcome by an evidence weight. Closed because every consumer must decide what to do with each state, and an unhandled fourth value would be a bug rather than a gap.

values.description: Every field the record kind declares required is present and well formed

Required fields are present, and something the source supplied could not be fully represented or something a consumer would expect is absent. The record remains usable; the reasons say what is missing

A required canonical field is missing or cannot be safely represented. The record is still stored, because a raw record that cannot be normalized is a fact someone has to be able to find -- but it must not be read as an observation

closed_enums.name: NormalizationQualityReason
closed_enums.description: Why a normalized record is not VALID. A closed vocabulary rather than free text, for the same reason AcquisitionErrorCode is one: a consumer branches on the MEANING -- a record with no reported value is skipped, a record whose geography is unclassified is still usable -- and a message it had to pattern-match would make that branch break on a reworded string.

values.description: The source published no figure for this metric, geography and period. A real statement by the source, not a failure, and NEVER represented as zero: zero is a measurement and absence is not

The source published something in the value position that could not be read as an exact decimal. Distinct from VALUE_NOT_REPORTED on purpose: one is the source saying nothing, the other is this system failing to read what it said

The source geography code has no entry in the reviewed geography map, so it is neither established as a country nor as an aggregate. The source code is preserved verbatim and no canonical code is assigned -- an unclassified code is never promoted to a country
The raw record carries no geography at all, so the observation cannot be placed. Renders the record INVALID
The raw record names no metric, so there is nothing the value is a measurement OF. Renders the record INVALID
The period is in a form this adapter does not represent. Renders the record INVALID rather than approximated: inventing an exact date the source did not give is how January 1 becomes an event time

The source published a period label with no timezone, and none has been established from its documentation. The bounds are recorded as wall-clock readings and `observed_at` is left null: a UTC offset the source never published would land in the field a consumer trusts most

The source language label has no established mapping to a canonical language tag. The label is preserved verbatim and no tag is assigned -- deriving one from a name is the same class of inference the geography map exists to replace

closed_enums.name: NormalizationErrorCode
closed_enums.description: Why a normalization attempt produced no record at all. Distinct from NormalizationQualityReason, which explains a record that EXISTS and is degraded. Closed so orchestration branches on a meaning rather than on a Python exception class, the same argument AcquisitionErrorCode makes.

values.description: No normalizer is registered for this source. Fails closed: an unknown source is never handed to whichever normalizer happens to exist

A normalizer exists for the source and does not declare support for the collector version that wrote the record. Refused rather than attempted, because a parse that half-works on an unknown shape is worse than one that stops

The raw record is missing something a record of its kind must have -- no payload, no provenance, no attribution obligation. Never repaired: the raw layer records what the source returned, and correcting it would destroy the evidence that it was wrong
The raw record's shape maps to no registered canonical record kind

A stored normalized record already exists for this exact identity -- same raw record, same schema version, same normalizer id and version -- and re-running produced DIFFERENT canonical content. Either the normalizer is not deterministic, or a reviewed input it reads changed without the version being bumped. Reported rather than written: overwriting would destroy the stored representation, and bumping the normalizer version is the mechanism by which output is allowed to change
A normalized record was produced and could not be stored. Nothing was committed
The job was cancelled or reached its batch bound before completing

closed_enums.name: NormalizedPeriodType
closed_enums.description: The temporal shape of a canonical observation. Closed because downstream time handling must branch exhaustively -- a YEAR is not an INSTANT, and code that treated the start of a yearly period as an exact event time would produce trend artifacts indistinguishable from real market movements (data-principles.md §9). An adapter supports only the forms its real records use and reports the rest rather than approximating them.

values.description: A calendar year. The start bound is January 1 and is NOT an event time
A calendar quarter
A calendar month
A calendar day
A point in time the source stated to timestamp resolution. The only value for which a single moment is the observation
An arbitrary interval the source stated explicitly, where no calendar unit describes it

closed_enums.name: NormalizedGeographyKind
closed_enums.description: What kind of entity a source geography code names. Closed because the branch is exhaustive and consequential: a COUNTRY can join to a MarketScope country list and an AGGREGATE must never be counted as one. UNKNOWN exists because it is the safe failure -- an unclassified code keeps its source form and is never promoted to a country.

values.description: A single country, established by an entry in the reviewed geography map. Only this kind carries a canonical ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
A group of countries or an income or regional grouping -- 'World', 'High income'. Preserved as an aggregate, never mapped to a country

Not established. The source code is preserved verbatim, no canonical code is assigned, and the record is PARTIAL. Guessing from the label would be inference, and inference is what the map exists to replace

closed_enums.name: NormalizedValueState
closed_enums.description: Whether a canonical numeric observation carries a measurement. Closed and mandatory because the alternative is representing 'the source published no figure' as the number zero -- and zero is a real measurement, so the two would become permanently indistinguishable with no way for any downstream stage to recover the difference.

values.description: The source published a figure, and the value holds it exactly
The source published no figure for this metric, geography and period. The value is null. The ordinary case for a sparse series, not a failure
The source published something that could not be read as an exact decimal. The value is null and the quality reasons record it

closed_enums.name: NormalizedUnitState
closed_enums.description: Whether a canonical numeric observation carries a unit, and why not when it does not. Closed so that 'the source does not publish units on this endpoint' stays distinguishable from 'we have not established the unit' -- the first is a settled fact about the access path and the second is work someone could do. Neither is ever resolved by reading the metric name.

values.description: The source published a unit, and it is recorded verbatim

The authorized access path does not carry a unit for this observation. Inferring one from the metric identifier would be a guess dressed as a fact, and the first metric whose naming convention differed would make it silently wrong
Not established. Reserved for an adapter whose source MAY publish a unit and did not for this observation

closed_enums.name: NormalizedTimezoneState
closed_enums.description: Whether the timezone of a canonical period's bounds is established. Closed because the branch is exhaustive and consequential: an ESTABLISHED period carries timezone-aware bounds and an event time, and a NOT_ESTABLISHED one carries wall-clock bounds and no event time at all. The distinction cannot be collapsed -- a source that publishes a bucket label and no offset is not the same as one that publishes UTC, and storing an aware datetime beside a note saying it is not really UTC would be a lie next to a disclaimer.

values.description: The source states the timezone, or authoritative documentation does. The period's bounds are timezone-aware and `observed_at` carries the start

The source publishes a period label and no offset, and none has been established. The bounds are naive wall-clock readings -- floating time -- and `observed_at` is null rather than an invented moment. Answering it later is a re-derivation over records already held, not a re-collection

closed_enums.name: NormalizedLanguageMapping
closed_enums.description: Whether a source language label has been mapped to a canonical language tag. Closed for the reason NormalizedGeographyKind is: the safe failure has to be nameable. A source publishing a human-readable language name is not publishing a language tag, and a name sitting in a field whose contract means a tag is a guess wearing the clothes of a fact. The source label is preserved either way.

values.description: A reviewed mapping assigns a canonical language tag to this source label. Only this state carries a tag
No reviewed mapping exists for this source label. The label is kept verbatim, no tag is assigned, and the absence stays visible rather than being resolved by resemblance

closed_enums.name: SignalQuantityFamily
closed_enums.description: What kind of quantity a derived Signal is about. Closed because consumers branch exhaustively on it and the families have different scope shapes -- a lexical signal carries a term and NO geography key, a series signal carries a metric and a geography -- so an unhandled third value is a bug rather than a gap. It is deliberately NOT DemandSignalFamily: PAIN/DESIRE/BEHAVIORAL/MARKET classify demand, and a count of how often a token occurred in news text is not evidence of demand. It is also not the registry called signal_family, which says what a SOURCE could expose (ADR-017). Three relations, three subjects, three names.

values.description: How often language tokens occur in text a source processed. Carries a term and a source language label, and no geography key at all
A numeric quantity a source measures or reports over a period. Carries a metric and a geography

closed_enums.name: SignalDirection
closed_enums.description: Which way the derived quantity moved. About CHANGE ONLY: POSITIVE and NEGATIVE are deliberately absent because they are sentiment, and a complaint-frequency signal can be INCREASING while the sentiment of the underlying text is negative -- one enum holding both would make that sentence unrepresentable. Any value other than NOT_APPLICABLE requires a temporal basis of ORDERED_PERIODS or COMPARABLE_INSTANTS, because increasing is a statement about before and after.

values.description: The quantity is larger at the later position
The quantity is smaller at the later position
Equal at both positions. Not STABLE: stability is a claim about variance over a window, which two points cannot support
The comparison ran and did not resolve to a direction -- a non-monotonic sequence, or a tie the derivation declines to break
The derivation states no ordered relation, so direction is not a question it answers. The only value permitted under a NONE or SAME_PERIOD_LABEL basis

closed_enums.name: SignalMagnitudeKind
closed_enums.description: How to read a Signal's magnitude. Closed because a ratio of 2 and a difference of 2 are not the same fact, and a consumer that could not tell them apart would compare them. There is no LEVEL value: a level is one observation, and one observation is not a Signal.

values.description: A difference expressed in the inputs' own quantity. The unit is INHERITED where the inputs published one and NOT_ESTABLISHED where they did not

A difference between two quantities measured at the SAME position -- two lexical terms in one source period, two geographies in one year. Distinct from ABSOLUTE_CHANGE because that one asserts something changed, which is a statement about time: a consumer branching on this value must be able to tell a contrast from a movement. The unit follows the inputs, as for ABSOLUTE_CHANGE
One quantity relative to another. Always DIMENSIONLESS
How many observations satisfied the derivation's condition. Always DIMENSIONLESS, and a diagnostic count rather than a sample size

closed_enums.name: SignalMagnitudeUnitState
closed_enums.description: Whether a Signal's magnitude carries a unit, and why not when it does not. The counterpart of NormalizedUnitState one layer up, and it exists for the same reason: GDELT publishes four columns and none is a unit, so a change over GDELT counts has no unit to inherit. Naming one here would assert the source did something it did not.

values.description: The contributing observations published a unit and the magnitude carries it verbatim. The only state that carries a unit string
The magnitude has no unit by construction -- a ratio, or a count of observations. Required for RATIO and OBSERVATION_COUNT
The magnitude is in the inputs' quantity and the inputs published no unit. Carried up rather than resolved

closed_enums.name: SignalTemporalBasis
closed_enums.description: What temporal relation a derivation actually used. Closed and consequential: ORDER and GLOBAL INSTANT are different questions needing different evidence, and collapsing them is how a timezone gets invented. Only COMPARABLE_INSTANTS may carry window bounds or leave observed_at non-null; every other basis carries neither.

values.description: The derivation relates its inputs without any temporal relation between them
Every input carries the identical source period label. String equality over a value the source published, needing no timezone -- the basis available to GDELT while H-29 is open
The inputs are placed in sequence within one source stream, without being placed on any shared timeline. Requires SOURCE_RELATIVE_ORDER
The inputs are placed on a shared timeline. Requires COMPARABLE_INSTANT, and is the only basis that carries timezone-aware window bounds

closed_enums.name: SignalRequiredFact
closed_enums.description: A canonical fact a derivation declares it needs. Closed because each value maps to a specific set of NormalizationQualityReason values that withhold it and to the record kinds that can supply it, so the check is mechanical rather than a judgement. The point is that PARTIAL must not automatically mean unusable: what matters is whether the SPECIFIC missing fact matters to the SPECIFIC derivation.

values.description: A reported figure readable as an exact decimal. Withheld by VALUE_NOT_REPORTED and MALFORMED_NUMERIC_VALUE
The source term, verbatim. Supplied only by lexical_frequency_observation
The source's own period label, for equality and membership. Needs no timezone; withheld only by PERIOD_NOT_SUPPORTED

The ability to say which of two observations came first within one source stream, without placing either on a shared timeline. Withheld by PERIOD_TIMEZONE_NOT_ESTABLISHED unless the source appears in the reviewed order certification, which is empty (H-32)
A moment on a timeline shared with other sources. Withheld by PERIOD_TIMEZONE_NOT_ESTABLISHED (H-29)
The source language label and its scheme, for equality within one source. Sufficient for within-source work while H-30 is open
A canonical language tag. Withheld by LANGUAGE_NOT_MAPPED, and required for any cross-source language aggregation (H-30)
A geography established as a country or an aggregate. Withheld by GEOGRAPHY_NOT_CLASSIFIED and GEOGRAPHY_MISSING

closed_enums.name: SignalDerivationKind
closed_enums.description: How a Signal was produced. Closed and mandatory so that a Signal not being inherently LLM-generated is a constraint rather than a sentence: DETERMINISTIC requires model and prompt versions to be ABSENT, and MODEL_DERIVED requires a model version.

values.description: Arithmetic and comparison over canonical values. Reproducible from the inputs and the parameters alone, with no model and no prompt
A model participated. Obliged to carry provider and model version, an extraction confidence, schema validation and untrusted-content handling (llm-reasoning-rules.md §7, §9)

closed_enums.name: SignalInputRole
closed_enums.description: Whether an input actually entered the derivation. Excluded inputs are recorded rather than dropped: we looked at ten and used six must be visible, and a signal that quietly used six of ten is indistinguishable from one that was offered six.

values.description: The input supplied every fact the derivation required and entered the result
The input was considered and set aside. Carries the reason and the facts it could not supply

closed_enums.name: SignalRefusalReason
closed_enums.description: Why an input was excluded, or why a whole derivation produced no Signal. One vocabulary for both, because a refused derivation is usually an exclusion having happened often enough. A refusal is a RETURNED VALUE, never a row: a record in a table of signals says a signal exists, and one meaning no signal exists is a misleading signal.

values.description: The normalized record is INVALID. A record that could not be represented must not be read as an observation
A canonical fact the derivation requires is absent, per the record's own quality reasons or its record kind

Two contributing rows carry the same observation_key under different lineages. Refused rather than resolved: choosing between them is D-08, which is open, and counting both would manufacture a contrast out of one observation
The inputs disagree on record kind or period resolution. Never silently coarsened to the coarser of the two

The inputs are the same record kind at the same resolution and are not observations of the same thing -- a different metric, geography, unit, dataset, source period label, source language label or gram size. INCOMPATIBLE_INPUT_KINDS cannot express this: two World Bank observations of different countries disagree on neither kind nor resolution. The detail names the field that disagreed

The inputs ARE the same series and their source period labels are not one documented step apart. Distinct from INCOMPATIBLE_SERIES, which says the observations are of different things, and from INSUFFICIENT_INPUT_OBSERVATIONS, which says there are too few: here there are two compatible observations and the interval between them is not the one the source publishes. Treating them as adjacent would invent continuity across a bucket nobody read, and a change computed across an invented gap is indistinguishable from one that happened
Fewer than two distinct source observations remain. One observation is not a Signal
The signal type is not registered, or its declared family does not match the inputs
A parameter affecting the output was not stated. A hidden default makes the extractor version meaningless

numeric_types.name: Confidence
numeric_types.description: How much the system trusts a value or interpretation. Presented as a percentage.

numeric_types.name: Probability
numeric_types.description: Likelihood of an event or outcome.

numeric_types.name: Independence
numeric_types.description: SUPERSEDED by EvidenceIndependenceState in Mission 1.2. A scalar cannot express WHICH records share an origin, so it could not support the grouping the aggregation framework requires, and it invited q * independence -- discounting instead of grouping, which lets ten discounted duplicates still outweigh one original. Retained so historical references resolve; no column uses it.

numeric_types.name: Score
numeric_types.description: An assessed magnitude. NOT interchangeable with Confidence.

numeric_types.name: EvidenceLevel
numeric_types.description: 0 Hypothesis, 1 Weak, 2 Repeated, 3 Multi-source, 4 Market evidence, 5 Direct validation. Never rescaled, never averaged into a score.

market_scope.canonicalization: Country codes uppercased, deduplicated, sorted. Region ids lowercased, deduplicated, sorted. One scope therefore has exactly one representation, which is what makes it safe as a cache key, a dedup key and an equality test.

research_context.note: Not an entity. No identity, no lifecycle. Serialized as an immutable snapshot on a ResearchSession.

blocked.what: Evidence aggregation formula, recency behaviour, independence handling, contradiction handling (RESOLVED AT FRAMEWORK LEVEL by Mission 1.1 -- evidence-aggregation-framework-v1.md)
blocked.consequence: The V1 algorithm is defined and has a reference implementation. Its PARAMETERS are not calibrated, so no CALIBRATED profile exists and services/scoring remains unavailable for production research. The rejected designs stay forbidden: no flat contradiction penalty, no per-item decay weight, no per-source reliability constant.

blocked.what: Source registry contents and per-source legal review records (RESOLVED by Mission 1.0 -- source-registry-v1.md)
blocked.consequence: Resolved globally: the registry, the review model and the eligibility gate exist. A source is still individually blocked until its own review passes, and collector_enabled defaults to false.
MarketScope stays geographic only. No SEGMENT variant.

blocked.what: Claim as a persisted entity (RESOLVED by Mission 1.2 -- opportunity-ontology-v2.1.md, claim-model-v1.md)
blocked.consequence: Resolved: research.claims exists with stable identity, append-only statement revisions, explicit temporality and provenance, and evidence now references a claim rather than an opportunity. Production scoring remains blocked for the separate reason that no CALIBRATED aggregation profile exists.
